title: Rescue Drone Engineering
alt: Thakorn operating a drone during an outdoor test beside the sea.
caption: Outdoor flight testing on the coast.
summary: Aerial support for emergency supply delivery and search-and-rescue operations.
overview: I designed, built, and iterated a rescue-drone prototype to explore how aerial systems can support emergency supply delivery and search and rescue. I focused on stability, endurance, payload performance, control response, and communication reliability.
process: Build and integrate
I developed the mechanical and electrical prototype, connecting flight control, camera-based perception, and a ground station. The report documents the architecture and software workflow below.
Test and revise
I completed 60 laboratory test flights and three outdoor field trials in Vung Tau and Dong Nai, using observations from each round to guide revisions.
Connect perception and response
The system combines person detection, pose analysis, and time-based alert logic with map-based telemetry to support rescue coordination.
note: The project also explored extended control through 4G connectivity. The drone remains a prototype; the reported operating figures describe the development work rather than a guaranteed rescue capability.
details: The prototype achieved 20–30 minutes of flight time and an approximately 3 km RC range, with extended control explored through 4G connectivity.
The technical report sets a maximum cargo weight of 5 kg within the project’s design scope. This is the documented design limit, rather than a measured payload result.

technical.title: From camera input to a rescue alert
technical.intro: The report connects mechanical design, flight control, onboard vision, and a ground-station interface into one prototype. The central engineering problem is turning a moving camera’s observations into an actionable location alert.
subsystems: Airframe & flight

An F650-based quadcopter modeled in SolidWorks combines a Pixhawk flight controller, GPS and inertial sensing, a Raspberry Pi, and a camera. The report describes PID attitude control, GPS-waypoint missions, and return-to-home landing.
Perception & tracking
YOLOv5 identifies people, SORT maintains tracks across frames, and MediaPipe Pose estimates body landmarks for each tracked person.
Behavior over time
The software examines an arm raised above the head, wrist movement, and elbow-angle changes. A timed state machine escalates persistent trigger conditions instead of relying on one video frame.
Operator interface

A Flask application with SocketIO brings together live video, a Leaflet map, waypoints, flight telemetry, and location alerts. The report describes mission pausing and coordinate transmission after an SOS trigger.
workflow: Find people in the camera feed and maintain a track for each person.
Compare wrist and head positions; calculate motion features from recent observations.
The report’s intermediate FROZEN state begins after 1.5 seconds; SOS begins after 3 seconds of a persistent trigger. These are software settings for the prototype.
Display the alert state and relay location information to the monitoring station for human follow-up.

evaluation.title: What the report evaluates
evaluation.intro: Chapter 5 reports the following observations. The report does not supply the raw evaluation dataset, sample counts, or a complete test protocol, so these figures are presented as report-stated results.
rows: GPS waypoint following
Typical path deviation under 0.6 m
Chapter 5 describes comparison with the planned GPS path using telemetry and mapped flight tracks.
Person detection
Over 95% in controlled tests
Reported for controlled person-detection tests using the vision and tracking pipeline.
Distress recognition
False-positive rate below 5%
Reported for the pose-and-time-based distress-recognition logic; separate from person detection.

technical.followup: The report identifies crowded scenes, weather and visibility, battery life, and onboard computation as constraints. A stronger evaluation would separate person detection from distress recognition, record false alarms across different conditions, and document the tested payload configuration.

title: Smart Life Jacket
alt: Annotated prototype photograph showing the life jacket, solar panel, electronics enclosure, LoRa antenna, and buoyant supports.
caption: Integrated prototype, reproduced from the SMARTVEST-SAR project report.
summary: GPS tracking, radio communication, and wind-informed drift prediction for water-rescue coordination.
overview: I developed a smart life-jacket prototype for water emergencies and flood-response scenarios. The system connects a wearable GPS and LoRa node, intermediate radio relays, and a Python rescue-station application. Its broader design goal is to help coordinate position information with drone-supported rescue.
process: Locate and transmit
The wearable firmware acquires GPS positions, buffers packets, and retains unacknowledged messages for retransmission over LoRa.
Relay and visualize
Intermediate nodes demonstrate store-and-forward communication. The Python application receives packets, plots recent positions, and retrieves local wind information.
Estimate drift
The current predictor combines recent GPS movement with wind direction using an explainable heuristic. It generates a possible short-term path; it is not a trained machine-learning model.
note: The prototype includes solar-assisted power and temperature-triggered heating logic. Radio range, battery endurance, thermal performance, and drift-prediction accuracy remain to be validated. It is an educational engineering prototype, not certified rescue equipment.
details: The system combines location tracking and drift-direction prediction to support coordination with rescue drones during water emergencies and flood-response operations.
missing: Measured radio range and packet-delivery results
Detailed individual hardware and software contributions
mentor: Associate Professor Dr. Le My Ha

diagram.title: SmartVest-SAR: tracking, communication, and power
diagram.alt: Supplied SmartVest-SAR diagram showing the GPS and wind-informed drift workflow, LoRa data packets, solar-assisted power, and prototype test stages.
diagram.caption: The supplied system diagram brings together tracking, radio communication, and power. The approximately 8 km LoRa hop shown is a design target, and the diagram identifies settings that still require validation.

technical.title: A wearable node, a radio relay, and a rescue-station app
technical.intro: SMARTVEST-SAR is an integrated engineering prototype. Its report traces the wearable firmware, intermediate relay firmware, and Python application to show how location data move from the jacket to an operator.
subsystems: Wearable sensing

The embedded firmware parses GPS fixes with TinyGPS++, reads a temperature sensor, and queues position messages. The code uses a 5-second GPS timer for bench testing and formats each packet as a device identifier plus latitude and longitude.
LoRa communication
The jacket sends the oldest queued message and waits up to one second for an “ok” acknowledgement. Unacknowledged messages remain queued for a later retry.
Intermediate relay
A relay stores unique received messages, forwards the oldest entry, and removes it after acknowledgement. This implements store-and-forward behavior; dynamic mesh routing remains a future step.
Rescue-station software
A Python/Tkinter application receives serial data in a background thread, acknowledges messages, removes duplicates, plots coordinates, and retrieves wind information through Open-Meteo.
Solar-assisted power
The integrated vest carries a solar panel and a lithium-battery subsystem. Solar charging is intended to supplement stored energy; continuous energy autonomy is not established by the report.
Temperature-triggered output

The firmware enables the heater output below a measured 25 °C and disables it at or above that value. This is a prototype control setting; independent thermal protection and fault-response testing are identified as further work.
technical.workflow_title: How the drift estimate is formed
workflow: Use the two latest GPS positions to estimate a recent movement direction.
Combine recent movement (70%), a weighted average of up to five wind-direction samples (20%), and current wind direction (10%).
Generate 20 future markers, gradually turning toward the target direction. These weights and the marker count are configured heuristics, not learned parameters.
Compare with a later measured track

The report proposes comparing predicted positions with a later recorded GPS track. It documents the prediction algorithm and visualization, while identifying quantitative prediction testing as a next step.
figures: Flowchart from report Figure 3.2 showing temperature sensing, GPS buffering, LoRa transmission, and acknowledgement retries.
Wearable firmware flow (report Figure 3.2). The 5-second GPS timer is a bench setting; the intended 5-minute reporting interval remains a design choice to test.
Flowchart from report Figure 3.3 showing duplicate checking and queued forwarding through an intermediate LoRa relay.
Relay firmware flow (report Figure 3.3). Duplicate checking and acknowledgement-based forwarding are implemented; a complete mesh protocol is not.

evaluation.title: Implementation and validation
evaluation.intro: The report provides a prototype photograph and code-level descriptions. It separates those implementation details from field performance that still needs measurement.
rows: GPS & radio
Position parsing, packet queue, acknowledgement, retry, and relay logic.
The approximately 8 km hop is a design target. Measured range, packet-delivery rate, and relay latency are not reported.
Solar-assisted power
A solar panel is visible on the integrated jacket; a battery subsystem is described.
Battery endurance and solar energy recovery have not been quantified in the report.
Temperature control
Firmware switches a heater output at a 25 °C sensor threshold.
The 25 °C value is a firmware setting. Independent surface-temperature and fault-response measurements are not reported.
Drift visualization
A deterministic movement-and-wind heuristic produces a projected path.
The report’s trajectory illustration is a software example. No measured prediction error against field tracks is reported.

technical.followup: The report proposes packet sequence numbers and timestamps, a bounded buffer, relay hop limits, independent thermal protection, and a measured energy budget. The approximately 8 km radio hop in the system diagram is a target awaiting field validation.
technical.source_note: Technical description: SMARTVEST-SAR report, Chapter 3, Sections 4.3–4.9, Chapter 5, and Appendix A. Coordination with rescue drones is the broader design goal; the report documents the wearable, relay, and desktop prototype.

title: AI, Finance, and the Vietnam Stock Market
alt: Thakorn presenting the AI, Finance, and the Vietnam Stock Market poster at SVIIF.
caption: Presenting the AI and Vietnam stock-market research poster at SVIIF.
summary: Investigating market signals, portfolio constraints, and risk through applied machine learning.
overview: As team leader, I directed an AI-driven study of Vietnam’s stock market, from data collection and model training to backtesting and presentation. The project received a Gold Medal at the Silicon Valley International Invention Festival in 2025.
process: Prepare the data
We collected 600 days of historical VPS API data for VIC, VNM, and VCB. The VIC prediction experiment used 10-day and 30-day moving averages, price change, daily price range, and lagged volume.
Model and backtest
The VIC experiment used a Decision Tree with a maximum depth of five and a 70% training / 30% test split. A daily price decline of at least 5% forced the predicted signal to ‘no buy’.
Account for constraints
Historical Value-at-Risk and portfolio-weight constraints were studied alongside Vietnam-specific trading assumptions, including settlement delays and daily price limits.
note: The poster presents separate prediction, allocation, and historical-backtesting experiments. Their results are shown by configuration below; expected returns from a backtest are not realized investment returns.
details: The poster documents 600 days of VPS API data for VIC, VNM, and VCB, with moving-average, price-change, price-range, and lagged-volume features for the VIC prediction task.
As SVIIF Team Leader, Thakorn directed model training, backtesting, and presentation, evaluating Decision Tree signals with a 5% stop-loss, historical Value-at-Risk, and portfolio-weight constraints.

research_results.title: Selected experiments from the poster
research_results.intro: Each row refers to a distinct experiment. The classifier accuracy, stock allocations, and strategy-backtest figures should be read in their own settings.

title: SafeFlow Vietnam
alt: A volunteer and a child assembling a small model boat in the Suoi Tuong floating classroom.
caption: Building a model together at the Suoi Tuong floating classroom.
summary: Connecting water safety, STEM learning, and practical support for flood-prone communities.
overview: I founded SafeFlow Vietnam to connect water-safety education, introductory STEM learning, and practical support for communities affected by water risk. I led two field programs in Y Tý, Lào Cai, a highland community exposed to recurring flash floods and landslides, and Suối Tượng, Đồng Nai, where families live in floating homes and daily life is closely tied to the water.
process: Learn from the setting
Each location shaped the program: Suối Tượng highlighted everyday life on the water, while Y Tý brought attention to the recurring risks of flash floods and landslides.
Teach and support
Activities combined water-safety education, hands-on STEM introductions, and the distribution of safety equipment and school supplies.
Mobilize resources
The two programs served approximately 200 students and residents, with more than VND 50 million mobilized in aid and programming.
details: Led two field programs serving approximately 200 students and residents in Y Tý, Lào Cai, and Suối Tượng floating village, Đồng Nai, with more than VND 50 million mobilized in aid and programming.

SafeFlow delivered water-safety education and introductory STEM activities, distributed safety equipment and school supplies, and connected rescue-drone and smart-life-jacket concepts with needs identified in flood-prone communities.

title: Creativism Club
alt: Thakorn speaking into a microphone beside a projected DRONEVERSE title slide.
caption: Sharing the process behind student engineering at DRONEVERSE.
summary: Public exhibitions and community CS & STEM programs that make technology accessible.
overview: As president of the 30-member Creativism Club, I connect student engineering with public learning and community outreach. I directed DRONEVERSE, a drone exhibition in Ho Chi Minh City that reached 500 people, and co-organized a CS & STEM program for 30 students from disadvantaged backgrounds at Darahoa charity classroom in Lam Dong.
process: DRONEVERSE: lead a shared platform
I directed DRONEVERSE in Ho Chi Minh City, a public exhibition bringing together drones, robotics, motors, computer science, and student engineering projects.
Connect with specialist knowledge
We partnered with IsLab, a laboratory specializing in drones and AI-enabled drone systems, for expert talks and technical demonstrations.
Share the process
As a featured student speaker, I explained the ideation, prototyping, and testing journey behind student-led drone and engineering projects.
Darahoa: co-organize community learning

I co-organized a CS & STEM program at Darahoa charity classroom in Lam Dong, introducing 30 students from disadvantaged backgrounds to computer science, logical thinking, and simple STEM experiments. The program distributed 30 gift packages with a total value of VND 10 million.
